theorem.name: WIDTH3_MLCR_MODEL_IS_POLYTIME_CONSTRUCTIBLE
theorem.statement: For every Boolean clause-set F in MLCR with maximum clause size at most 3, a satisfying assignment for F can be computed in deterministic polynomial time.
proof: Let n=n(F), m=c(F), and k=delta(F)=sigma(F)>=1. By the MLCR definition, mu_vd(F)>nM(k), hence integrality gives mu_vd(F)>=nM(k)+1.
Because every clause has size at most 3, the sum of all variable degrees equals the total number of literal occurrences and is at most 3m=3(n+k). Therefore n*(nM(k)+1)<=3(n+k).

If k>=2, the non-Mersenne sequence satisfies nM(k)>=k+2. Hence n*(k+3)<=3(n+k), so nk<=3k and therefore n<=3. These cases are solved constructively by testing at most 2^3=8 Boolean assignments and scanning the clauses.
If k=1, F is matching-lean and delta(F)=1. For matching-lean clause-sets, maximal deficiency delta*(F)=delta(F), hence delta*(F)=1.

MLCR is a subclass of SAT by Kullmann-Zhao Lemma 10.6. By the matching-deficiency result of Kullmann (Corollary 4.9/4.10 in the cited clausal-form development), every satisfiable F with delta*(F)=1 has a partial assignment phi using at most one variable such that phi*F is matching satisfiable.

Enumerate the empty partial assignment and the 2n one-variable Boolean assignments. For each phi, simplify F and test matching satisfiability by maximum bipartite matching. When a positive case occurs, compute a matching-satisfying assignment psi for phi*F and output phi composed with psi. Existence is guaranteed by the preceding theorem; all operations are polynomial.

complexity.k_ge_2: O(8*|F|) after computing the MLCR parameters; n<=3.
complexity.k_eq_1: At most 2n+1 matching-satisfiability tests plus simplification; polynomial in the encoded size of F.
complexity.uniformity: The case distinction uses k=delta(F), directly computable from m-n for MLCR inputs.

extension_to_conjecture_10_3_width3.statement: Kullmann-Zhao Conjecture 10.3 holds for Boolean clause-sets of maximum clause size at most 3.
proof: Given F with sigma(F)>=1 and mu_vd(F)>nM(sigma(F)), compute in polynomial time a minimal nonempty V with delta(F[V])=sigma(F) as in Lemma 10.8.
Theorem 10.9 gives F[V] in MLCR. Since F[V] is a sub-clause-set of F, maximum clause size remains at most 3.
Apply WIDTH3_MLCR_MODEL_IS_POLYTIME_CONSTRUCTIBLE to obtain a satisfying assignment on F[V].
By the autarky correspondence used in Lemma 10.1/Theorem 10.2, this assignment is a nontrivial autarky for F.
Thus the witness autarky required by Conjecture 10.3 is constructible in polynomial time on width-at-most-3 Boolean clause-sets.

TRUMP_primitive.name: WIDTH3_SURPLUS_DEGREE_PROOF_CARRYING_AUTARKY_STEP
TRUMP_primitive.input_condition: sigma(F)>=1 and mu_vd(F)>nM(sigma(F)) on a Boolean CNF of maximum width <=3
TRUMP_primitive.output: A concrete nontrivial autarky phi and the satisfiability-equivalent residual phi*F.
TRUMP_primitive.strict_progress: The autarky is nontrivial and removes at least one touched variable/at least one clause; the reduction loop can be charged by a decreasing variable/clause count.
TRUMP_primitive.scope: Conditional progress primitive only. It does not apply once the surplus/min-degree violation disappears and is not a universal 3SAT decider.

sources: Oliver Kullmann and Xishun Zhao, Bounds for variables with few occurrences in conjunctive normal forms, Theorem 10.2, Conjecture 10.3, Lemma 10.6, Lemma 10.8, Theorem 10.9

Oliver Kullmann, Constraint Satisfaction Problems in Clausal Form I: Autarkies and Deficiency, matching satisfiability and bounded maximal-deficiency construction, especially Corollaries 4.9, 4.10, 4.21

next_admissible_math.question: After exhausting matching-autarky, BCE and the now proof-carrying width-3 surplus/degree autarky step, can every nonterminal residual 3CNF be forced into another exact polynomial descent condition, or can an explicit infinite residual family be proved to survive the combined closure?
